```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M1"], "fault": "M5 (tail current source) is undersized: W=3.436 um at L=0.815 um gives a 3.0x mirror ratio over M6, so the tail carries only ~30 uA. This lowers gm1 (ugbw) and leaves M5 at Vds-Vdsat = 0.031 V, near triode. Upsizing M5 W (lowers Vdsat, raises tail current) would fix both."}
```

The ranking follows the sensitivities. ugbw is most sensitive to M5 and settling is most sensitive to M6 (its bias partner). M1 is a weaker third candidate, since its width only affects settling and it sits in weak inversion. The mirror ratio is consistent with M5 and M6 as drawn, so the fault is not uniquely determined from these numbers alone; M6 is a plausible alternative if the reference device was the one altered.
